_readme: EVERY PIECE OF THE SITE'S FURNITURE, IN ONE PLACE.
The writings, the concepts, the topic descriptions and the manual sheets are
content and live in the graph or in data/notes.json. This file holds the
other kind of text: the words the site says about itself. The two doors and
what they promise, the line under his name, the headings above a list, the
words on the buttons that carry you back.
It exists so that changing any of them is editing a value rather than
editing a program. Before this, a sentence like 'Everything I have built so
far' could only be changed by someone willing to open an HTML file and find
it, which meant it could only be changed by asking.
HOW IT REACHES THE PAGE. Markup carries data-t="key" and is filled at boot;
text built in JavaScript calls T('key'). Nothing is duplicated between the
two, and tools/textcheck.js refuses a build where a key is used and missing,
or present and unused - the first renders a blank space on the page, and the
second is a value someone will edit expecting it to do something.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, and deliberately. The threshold's two count lines are
derived from the graph itself - '15 topics, 153 objects' - and a person
editing those by hand would be writing a number that the mind could then
contradict. They are computed, and the only honest way to change them is to
change what they count.
